A.explanation: The combined regime is severe. The parent framework bars legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care, so a trans visitor's documents stay as issued and cannot be aligned. Extremism and propaganda statutes are enforced, with 101 convictions, club raids and a documented death in pretrial custody. The occupied peninsula adds a further operative layer: a propaganda law for all audiences, a 12-year extremism exposure, militia and occupation-leadership threats, a documented lure-and-assault of a foreigner with no police recourse, and barred monitors. No protective machinery operates for visitors. Imprisonment, custody harm and street violence are all documented, and remedies are absent. The rating sits in the Severe band, below the parent-level case because the territorial layer adds exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport and visa gender markers cannot be changed; a 2023 law bans marker change and surgery, so mismatch with presentation is unresolved and exposed at any checkpoint.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at entry can lead into police questioning under extremism and propaganda enforcement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Extremism-related arrests and detention; a man arrested over an LGBT travel business was found dead in pretrial detention (Dec 2024).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention on extremism or propaganda charges carries documented lethal risk with no custodial safeguards shown.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent national regime applies; the peninsula is under the occupying state's full regime, including propaganda law for all audiences and a 12-year extremism exposure.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Territorial and parent rules stack; the harsher operative rule governs.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming medical care banned (2023 in the occupying regime and national law); legal gender-change procedures unusable under occupation.
care_services.interaction: Care denial combines with document inability and detention risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Occupation leadership threatened LGBT people that police and self-defence forces will react to any gay street presence; militia threatened to expel LGBT people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing links police action with militia pressure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Propaganda law bars material giving minors a desire to change sex; a child travelling with a trans parent faces family-level exposure to enforcement and disclosure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Propaganda enforcement reaches content a family may carry; guardian investigation is possible.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented lure-and-assault of a foreigner via a fake dating profile, filmed and published; violent attacks on LGBT people; almost all openly LGBT residents have fled.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police recourse for the assaulted foreigner not available.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Predation is compounded by the absence of police response and by police threat-framing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection; hate motivation not aggravating; hate crimes not recorded; international monitors barred.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Victims face no operative route to remedy, so outing or assault leads to unremedied harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.15-A in pretrial custody with beatings, confiscated phones and blocked outside contact, and in no effective appeal. A lies slightly higher because no capital charging or execution is documented for presentation cases. The occupied peninsula's militia threats and documented lure-assault keep it close to the 0.15 tier.

Higher-risk than 0.35-A, which involves routine exclusion and humiliation without arrest or lethal custody. A documents imprisonment exposure, a custody death and a documented predation and assault pattern with no police recourse, which is more severe than discretionary refusal.

Substantially lower than 0.55-B, which describes administrative friction, remedies that work partially and no credible path toward detention or execution. A has enforced criminal and extremism exposure, documented custody death and no operative remedy.

A would need legal gender recognition or marker-change access, lawful care, no enforced extremism or propaganda exposure, police and courts that act for trans victims, and no occupation-based threats. None of these is documented, so A is far below the 0.75-C level.

A.synthesis: The parent regime imposes universal exposure: documents cannot be aligned, care is banned, and propaganda and extremism enforcement reaches expression and venues. The occupied peninsula adds militia threats, a documented predation and assault pattern, and barred monitors. Detention is documented as lethal, and no remedy operates. A visitor who is outed or detained therefore faces custody and violence with no recourse, which places the jurisdiction in the Severe band.

B.explanation: The combined regime is the national framework only; the division record adds no state-specific layer. Same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023, and propaganda enforcement carries fines and detention, with repeated offences exposed to criminal prosecution. Extremism convictions reach 101 with up to 12 years, and a man died in pretrial detention in Dec 2024. The 2023 transition law voids marriages on birth-sex grounds. No division-specific protection or remedy is documented, and no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse exists. The rating sits in the Severe band, marginally above A because no occupation-specific threats or documented predation pattern is recorded in the dossier.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport and visa markers cannot be changed under a 2023 law; mismatch with presentation persists for any visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at entry can trigger questioning under propaganda or extremism enforcement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Extremism and propaganda arrests; 81 administrative guilty findings for displaying banned symbols; death in pretrial detention documented (Dec 2024).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention carries documented lethal risk without shown safeguards.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National framework governs the division; no division-specific rule or finding is recorded, so the national regime is the operative regime.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational layer adds or offsets the national exposure.

care_services.exposure: Trans-specific healthcare effectively banned in 2023; gender transition banned.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National propaganda law punishes public expression promoting gender transition; 257 penalties imposed in 2023-24 against 22 in 2021-22.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement is national; the division-level record shows no difference.

minors_guardians.exposure: Propaganda law applies to all ages and bars material giving minors a desire to change sex; families face exposure through disclosure and enforcement.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian presence does not shield a child from propaganda-based enforcement.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National club raids and arrests documented; no division-specific violence or predation record.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Enforcement reach is national; local street-level risk is not measured.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection; hate motivation not aggravating; hate crimes not officially recorded.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No operative remedy for victims of discrimination or assault.

anchor_checks.comparison: Close to 0.15-A in the sense of a propaganda-and-extremism regime with a custody death and no effective recourse. B lacks documented beatings, confiscated phones or torture in custody, so it sits a little higher than 0.15-A.
Similar to 0.35-A in universal document and care exposure. B adds enforced criminal and extremism exposure and a custody death, which places it lower than 0.35-A's discretionary exclusion regime.
Lower than 0.55-B, which offers partial remedies, bounded detention and no criminal exposure. B has criminal exposure and documented lethal custody without remedy.
B would need lawful care access, document accommodation at entry, no criminal propaganda or extremism enforcement and operative anti-discrimination recourse. None is documented.

B.synthesis: The division has no subnational rules or findings, so the national regime governs the traveller's exposure. It imposes universal document-mismatch risk, a care ban, criminal propaganda exposure, extremism prosecutions and a documented custody death. Remedies for discrimination or assault are not documented. The absence of a division-specific record is not mitigating. The result is a Severe-band rating close to A's parent regime, without A's occupation-layer threats.
